Where the junk goes

Donation drop first, recycling for metal and electronics, landfill last. We sort it so you do not have to.

  • Junk removal: Garage piles, old furniture and move-out leftovers loaded and sorted.
  • Donation runs: Usable furniture and boxes taken to local donation centers, with a receipt when they give one.
  • Appliance haul-away: Old fridges, washers and stoves disconnected, carried out and taken to metal recycling.

From the new house

Local moves Durham
"Moving out of a third-floor walk-up off Ninth Street in July heat. Two guys, and the third showed up at 10 when they saw the stairs. Every box had a tag and a room. I found the coffee maker in the kitchen of the new place before I found my shoes."
— Priya K. Sample review
Take apart and put back together Carrboro
"They took apart a bunk bed I had given up on and taped the bolts to the rails in labelled bags. Put it back together in the new room in twenty minutes."
— Marcus B. Sample review
Furniture and heavy items Hillsborough
"Our upright piano had to come down five brick porch steps. They laid boards, strapped it to a board dolly and walked it down slowly while one of them called out each step. Not a scratch on the steps or the piano."
— Helen W. Sample review
Junk removal Chapel Hill
"After closing on Dad's house we had a garage full of forty years of stuff. They set aside the tools my brother wanted, took two loads to donation and hauled the rest. Took one long morning."
— Dwayne T. Sample review
Local moves Morrisville
"Quoted four hours for our two-bedroom in Morrisville, took four and a half because of the elevator wait. They told us at hour three, not at the end. That's all I wanted."
— Erin S. Sample review
Labor-only loading Cary
"Hired them only to load a rental truck going to Ohio. They built the load like a wall, heaviest pieces to the front. Opened it in Columbus and nothing had moved."
— Ben O. Sample review
